title: Teach Me, O Teach Me, Lord! Thy Way
description: Teach Me, O Teach Me, Lord! Thy Way in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 477 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Divine Guidance”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Teach me, O teach me, Lord! thy way; So, to my life's re-mo-test day, By thy un-err-ing pre-cepts led, My will-ing feet its paths shall tread.

lines: Teach me, O teach me, Lord! thy way;
So, to my life's remotest day,
My willing feet its paths shall tread.
Informed by thee, with sacred awe,
My heart shall meditate thy law;
To thee its full obedience yield.
Give me to know thy will aright, —
Thy will, my glory and delight. —
That, raised above the world, my mind
In thee its highest good may find.
O turn from vanity mine eye;
To me thy quickening strength supply;
And with thy promised mercy cheer
A heart devoted to thy fear.

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
